name: Hair Fall
description: Hair fall is a common concern among individuals of all ages and can be caused by various factors such as genetics, hormonal changes, medical conditions, stress, and lifestyle choices.
causes: Hormonal imbalances (e.g., thyroid disorders, polycystic ovary syndrome)
Nutritional deficiencies (e.g., iron, protein, vitamins A, D, E)
Alopecia areata (an autoimmune disorder causing patchy hair loss)
risk_factors: Age (common in menopausal women and older adults)
Use of harsh chemical treatments or heat styling tools
recommended_product_categories: Shampoos and conditioners containing biotin or amino acids
Hair serums and oils with collagen and omega-3s

daily_routine.step: Gentle scalp massage before washing hair
daily_routine.purpose: Improves blood circulation to the scalp, promoting healthy hair growth

daily_routine.step: Use mild shampoo and lukewarm water for cleaning
daily_routine.purpose: Prevents harsh chemicals from stripping natural oils and causing dryness or irritation

natural_remedies: Aloe vera application to the scalp
Application of hibiscus or onion juice
Use of egg yolk mask for hair nourishment
lifestyle_tips: Manage stress through meditation or yoga
Eat a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals
Avoid tight hairstyles that pull on the scalp
Limit use of heat styling tools and chemical treatments
common_myths: Hair fall is always due to poor hygiene
Wearing a hat causes hair loss
Trimming your hair prevents it from falling out
when_to_consult_doctor: If hair fall persists despite changes in lifestyle and diet, or if there are sudden or extensive hair losses.
prevention: Maintain a healthy diet with essential nutrients
Use gentle hair care products and tools
Get regular check-ups for underlying health conditions

severity_levels.mild: Noticeable increase in daily hair fall, no visible bald patches.
severity_levels.moderate: Hair thinning with visible bald spots or noticeable hair loss.
severity_levels.severe: Significant hair loss leading to large bald areas on the scalp.

expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist if you notice any unusual changes in your hair fall pattern.
Keep track of your hair care routine and lifestyle habits for better diagnosis and treatment planning.
